findings.problem: Native global gridex_get_user_permissions direct_permissions lacks status/is_active/effect filters; a direct DENY row joined through permission_id becomes a positive candidate. No catalog or global/current-scope negative filter follows. gridex_has_permission then treats candidate membership as permission.
findings.actual_path: Native authenticated table ACLs and RLS policies on price_areas/price_area_localities use gridex_has_permission; these two tables have no restrictive current-session/tenant policies in inspected native metadata. No actual business call or user-row configuration needed to establish the definition-level incorrect precedence.
findings.fix: Global helper retains original role/direct/platform-fallback branches, requires direct active ALLOW and active catalog, filters global DENY plus each candidate grant own company DENY. A foreign company DENY cannot revoke a legitimate grant in another company for shared data.

findings.problem: Actual scoped context returns role ALLOW despite current global/company direct DENY, valid override DENY or inactive permission catalog. Older company helper likewise omits catalog/current negative precedence.
findings.fix: Integrates qualified Admin query correction; scoped helper filters candidate array using exact global/selected-company DENY predicates from actually applied actor oracle without its operational-company gate. Paused/history read semantics preserved.

findings.problem: Node API skipped all requirements for platform admins; filtering ordinary context.permissions alone cannot make explicit current denial/catalog unavailability outrank platform authority.
findings.fix: Add internal context active_permission_keys and denied_permissions. Platform effective requirement candidates are active catalog minus current negatives; ordinary candidates intersect that with context.permissions. Existing anyOf/allOf semantics retained, unknown/inactive catalog keys refused. Required fields absent and requirement nonempty =>503; empty requirement preserves base Admin behavior. No public/frozen API DTO keys changed.

findings.problem: Entity APIs resolve required permissions for cookie company before learning actual entity company, then platform entity helper skips company binding. A denial for actual other company could be missed.
findings.fix: API-only WeakMap records requirement and client; private enumerable symbol references original guard, surviving object spread without leaking through JSON. Entity guard revalidates native context for actual company before platform return; operational/readable helpers revalidate actual resolved company. Page guards retain existing policy. Repository search found direct original access.guard passing on current entity APIs and no spread/destructured guard copies; copied guard regression verifies retained requirement.

findings.problem: Native permission list/wrapper decisions did not re-evaluate current canonical Auth/profile state and could use permission rows for deleted/banned/inactive identities.
findings.fix: Reuse exact canonical context identity invariant (undeleted Auth user, wall-clock unbanned, confirmed email, active user_profile). No auth.uid equality restriction on service-supplied target IDs; legitimate service actor remains allowed. No invented deleted/disabled metadata fields, no new operational-company gate. Dynamic clock-dependent five functions become VOLATILE.
